prompt: Design an AI personal trainer app — an adaptive workout coach that builds daily routines, tracks reps sets and personal records, and adjusts your plan as you progress. It needs a home dashboard with today's session and readiness score, a library of guided exercises with form cues, and a progress screen with strength curves and milestones. Make it feel motivating, modern, and personal.
title: Repwise

issues.description: The verified detail screen defines generic geometric SVG scenes rather than exercise-specific static form images. This does not adequately support the brief's form guidance requirement for setup, execution, and common mistakes.

The detail composition must have one conversion point: gallery, one summary/action card, then divided facts and activity rows. The prescribed detail structure includes both a sticky detail pane and a separate CTA band, which risks creating competing primary actions and violates the single summary-card pattern.

Buttons define hover and focus-ring classes but do not define a visible active or pressed state. The primary hover class is also identical to its base class, so it provides no perceptible hover feedback.
The shared card component hardcodes rounded-xl, p-6, pt-0, and space-y-1.5 instead of using the theme radius and spacing ladder. The 6px vertical gap also breaks the required 8px grid.

The home screen's scene assets are generated SVG illustrations rather than the photo-first, human visual treatment required by the Airbnb design language. Use relevant training photography or clearly authored exercise imagery for catalog heroes and tiles.
Button sizing uses rounded-md for all controls, while the selected design language calls for pill-shaped solid coral primary actions and restrained hairline outline secondaries.

The avatar text uses var(--card-foreground), but that semantic token is not part of the provided token set. This can produce an undefined color and violates the requirement that all colors come from defined theme tokens.

The screen reads as an Airbnb listing rather than a single-item fitness detail page. “3:39/km,” “Dates,” “Guests,” “Verified host,” “Guest reviews,” and “Check availability” are booking concepts and are not appropriate for an adaptive personal trainer.

The detail view represents a 5K tempo run, while the product brief centers on adaptive workouts, strength changes, set/rep logging, suggested loads, PRs, and exercise form guidance. It does not explain why this workout was chosen or how it adapts.

The Airbnb-inspired structure is recognizable, but the abstract neon illustrations do not satisfy the stated photo-first, human, trust-building language. They also do not communicate exercise form or coaching cues.
There is a very large, empty-looking gap between the gallery and the workout title/summary. The page loses hierarchy and feels unfinished despite the otherwise clean alignment.
“Available,” “Flexible dates,” “2 guests,” “Johan Okafor,” and “Guest reviews” are specific but belong to a lodging marketplace, not a workout coach. The copy is not on-voice for Repwise.
The catalog is dominated by running sessions and pace metrics. Critical strength-training concepts—weight, reps, sets, rest, readiness, adaptive adjustments, and PR detection—are absent.
The daily-session hero is too sparse and its key metric, 8.0 km, is not presented at true hero scale. The duplicated Start session buttons compete instead of establishing one dominant action.

After the sparse white hero and toolbar, the page becomes a repetitive six-card grid with nearly identical image, metadata, divider, pace, and rating structures. It feels assembled from a catalog template rather than authored around one adaptive training story.

Rounded cards, coral actions, and generous whitespace loosely reflect the selected Airbnb language, but the colorful abstract artwork and SaaS-style top bar lack the warm, photo-first human quality of the references.

reviewResult.summary: The build respects the two-file screen boundary and uses relevant fitness-oriented scaffolding, but it is not ready for approval. The detail media is not specific enough for exercise coaching, the detail conversion architecture risks multiple competing actions, and shared components violate active-state, spacing, radius, and token-discipline requirements. Airbnb's photo-first and pill-button signatures are also underrepresented.
requiredFixes: In src/screens/detail.jsx, replace the generic inline SVG scene set with exercise-specific static form imagery for the single detail item, including step labels and setup/execution cues.

In src/screens/detail.jsx, keep the detail conversion point inside one deliberate summary card containing the selected exercise, targets, and the primary action. Remove any competing standalone CTA treatment.

In src/components/Button.jsx, add a visible pressed/active state for every button variant and ensure primary, secondary, and outline controls use the coral Airbnb token treatment with pill-shaped primary buttons.
In src/components/Card.jsx, replace hardcoded rounded-xl, p-6, pt-0, and space-y-1.5 classes with the theme radius and spacing tokens required by the 8px rhythm.
In src/components/Avatar.jsx, replace var(--card-foreground) with a defined theme token such as var(--foreground), or add a valid semantic token to the theme before using it.

detail: Rework the page into a genuine single-workout detail view: replace Airbnb-style pricing, dates, guests, host, availability, and “Guest reviews” language with workout summary, target pace/load, duration, readiness impact, exercise or interval breakdown, and a clear “Start workout” action.
detail: Replace the repeated abstract track illustrations with a coherent gallery of the same workout’s form or coaching visuals, using real static exercise images and specific captions/cues.

detail: Remove the excessive blank vertical gap between the gallery and workout summary; pull the summary and action card into the primary content flow while preserving generous but intentional spacing.

home: Make the dominant moment a clear adaptive daily-session scoreboard with hero-scale readiness, session focus, and next-target information; reduce the duplicated “Start session” controls to one primary action.

home: Add concrete strength-training content from the brief—sets, rep ranges, suggested load, rest duration, readiness inputs, PRs, and adaptive-plan explanation—instead of presenting an almost entirely running-focused catalog.
home: Introduce stronger surface and section variation. The page currently stacks a sparse white hero, toolbar, and a large uniform card grid with little authored composition or tonal separation.
home: Replace generic workout-card metadata such as pace-only values with useful trainer information including muscle group, equipment, difficulty, planned sets/reps, and completion state.
